video_caption: The video segment displays a static computer desktop, which appears to be running Windows 10, characterized by its default blue wallpaper featuring a glowing Windows logo on the right side. Several application icons are visible on the left side of the desktop, including "This PC," "Recycle Bin," multiple "Google Chrome" icons, "ShareX," "Wondershare Filmora," "Orbit," and "RAMESH 207 ATS." The Windows 10 taskbar is present at the bottom, featuring a "Type here to search" bar on the left, various pinned application icons, and system tray icons on the right, which show the date "15/08/2017" and time "10:38." In the top right corner of the screen, a colorful logo with the text "WINSTON TV" is displayed. A male voice narrates throughout the segment, saying, "What's up guys? You're watching another easy tutorial. Today I'm going to show you how to speed up your Windows 10 for free and without using any..." The video shows no people or significant visual changes, maintaining a consistent view of the desktop.

The video opens to a Windows 10 desktop screen with a blue background featuring the Windows logo. The Start menu is active on the left side, displaying a list of applications under categories like "Recently added" and "Most used," along with a grid of app tiles including Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Photos, News, Skype, Twitter, Minecraft, Get Office, and OneNote. A search bar is visible at the bottom left. In the top right corner of the screen, a watermark displays "Eager TV" next to a multicolored logo. The taskbar at the bottom of the screen shows various application icons and the current date and time (15/08/2017 19:39).

The video opens with a static shot of a Windows 10 desktop, featuring a blue background with a stylized Windows logo. Several desktop icons are visible on the left, including "This PC," "Recycle Bin," "Google Chrome," "SHAREit," "Wondershare Filmora," "Orbit," and "RAMESH 3997 ATS." At 0:03, a teal and white banner appears at the bottom of the screen with the text "02 Start Up Apps," indicating the topic. A mouse cursor then appears and right-clicks on the taskbar at the bottom of the screen, opening a context menu. "Task Manager" is selected from this menu, and a Task Manager window opens, initially showing the "Processes" tab with CPU, Memory, Disk, and Network usage details. The cursor then navigates to and clicks the "Startup" tab. This tab displays a list of applications configured to run at system startup, showing their names, publishers, current status (Enabled or Disabled), and startup impact. At 0:11, a red and green banner appears on the right side of the screen with the text "SUBSCRIBE FOR MORE VIDEOS." The user then selects "Orbit Downloader" which is currently "Enabled," and clicks the "Disable" button at the bottom right of the Task Manager window, changing its status to "Disabled." Next, "Wondershare Studio" is selected and similarly disabled. During this process, a voiceover advises viewers to "Make sure do not disable antivirus or Microsoft apps," and the cursor briefly highlights "npa-4" and "Microsoft OneDrive" which are enabled and published by "Bic Secure Labs Pvt. Ltd." and "Microsoft Corporation" respectively. The cursor returns to "Wondershare Studio," which is now "Disabled." Finally, the Task Manager window is closed, returning to the desktop.

The video segment opens with a Windows 10 desktop featuring a blue-themed wallpaper, overlaid with a graphic containing a yellow circle, a pink arrow, and the text "03 Defragment" (English). A male voice introduces the third step: defragmentation. The screen then shows the user clicking the Start Menu in the bottom-left corner, revealing the Windows 10 Start Menu with various application tiles and a search bar. Following the voice instruction to type "defragment and optimize drives," the user types "defr" into the search bar. The search results immediately display "Defragment and Optimize Drives" (English) listed as a "Desktop app" (English), which the user then selects. This action opens the "Optimize Drives" window, showing a list of hard drives (C:, D:, E:, F:, and a volume drive). The C: drive, labeled "Hard disk drive" (English) and indicated as "OK (0% fragmented)" (English), is highlighted. The voice explains that the C: drive, where the operating system is installed, needs to be selected. The user clicks the "Optimize" button, and the status for the C: drive changes to "Running... 61% analyzed" (English), then "Running... 70% analyzed" (English), "Running... 83% analyzed" (English), and finally "Running... Pass 1: 0% defragmented" (English), followed by "Running... Pass 1: 0% consolidated" (English), indicating the defragmentation process is underway or has completed its first pass. The voice notes that the process will take a few minutes. Once the process is seemingly complete, the user clicks the "Close" button, and the "Optimize Drives" window disappears, returning to the desktop screen.

The video segment opens with a view of a computer screen displaying a Windows "This PC" window, showing several folders and three local disk drives labeled (C:), (E:), and (F:). The mouse cursor is initially hovering over "Local Disk (C:)," which shows "101 GB free of 146 GB." The user then right-clicks on "Local Disk (C:)," causing a context menu to appear with various options like "Open," "Format...," and "Properties." The cursor moves down the menu and clicks on "Properties." This action opens a new "Local Disk (C:) Properties" window, displaying tabs such as "General," "Security," and "Tools," with the "General" tab selected. This tab shows details of the C drive, including the file system (NTFS), used space (45.0 GB), free space (101 GB), and total capacity (146 GB), visualized by a blue and gray pie chart. At the bottom of this window, a "Disk Cleanup" button is visible, along with two unchecked options: "Compress this drive to save disk space" and "Allow files on this drive to have contents indexed in addition to file properties."

The video segment opens with a Windows 10 desktop, featuring a blue background with a white window logo and various application icons on the left side, including "This PC", "Recycle Bin", "Google Chrome", and others. An overlay at the bottom left shows a yellow circle with the text "05 Visual Settings". The mouse cursor, represented by a white arrow, is initially near the bottom-left corner. At 0:04, the mouse clicks the Start button (Windows logo) on the taskbar, opening the Start Menu which includes a search bar at the bottom. The user then types "sys" into the search bar. As the letters are typed, the search results update dynamically on the left side of the Start Menu, showing options like "System Information" (Desktop app) as the "Best match" and "System" under the "Settings" category. The mouse cursor moves and hovers over "System" within the "Settings" section, highlighting it in grey, and remains in that position until the end of the segment.

The video begins with a view of a Windows 10 desktop featuring icons such as "This PC," "Recycle Bin," "Google Chrome," "SHAREit," "Wondershare Filmora," and "Orbit," with a blue default wallpaper and an "Eager TV" logo in the top right corner. A text overlay at the bottom left reads "06 Temparary Files Dlt" (06 Temporary Files Delete), indicating the topic of the video. The user then opens the Start menu, briefly revealing various app tiles, before typing "run" into the search bar and selecting the "Run" desktop app. During this action, a prominent red text overlay "SUBSCRIBE FOR MORE VIDEOS" (SUBSCRIBE FOR MORE VIDEOS) appears on the right side of the screen, serving as a call to action. The "Run" dialog box opens, and the user types "%temp%" (percent temp percent), which is also highlighted in red text on the screen, into the "Open:" field before clicking "OK." This action opens a File Explorer window displaying the contents of the "Temp" folder, with the path "HYR > AppData > Local > Temp" visible at the top. The user then presses "Ctrl+A" (Control A), shown as red text on the right, to select all items within the folder, followed by a right-click to initiate deletion. A brief progress window titled "Recycling 777 items from Temp" appears, immediately followed by a "Folder In Use" dialog box stating, "The action can't be completed because the folder or a file in it is open in another program." The user clicks "Skip" to proceed, leaving one remaining item, "CamRec0," in the folder. The video concludes as the user closes the File Explorer window, returning to the initial Windows 10 desktop screen.

The video opens with a Windows 10 desktop displaying icons like "This PC," "Recycle Bin," "Google Chrome," "SHAREit," "Wondershare Filmora," and "Orbit," with the date and time "15/08/2017 11:35" visible on the taskbar. The user clicks the Start menu, types "run" in the search bar, and selects the "Run" desktop app. A "Run" dialog box appears, and the word "temp" (TEM P) in red text flashes on the screen as the user types "temp" into the "Open" field of the dialog box, then clicks "OK." A "Temp" folder access warning appears, and the user clicks "Continue." The "Temp" folder opens, displaying numerous files. The text "Ctrl+A" in red flashes on the screen as the user selects all the files in the folder (Ctrl+A) and then right-clicks and chooses "Delete," making the folder empty. The screen returns to the desktop, and the user again clicks the Start menu, types "run," and selects the "Run" desktop app. The "Run" dialog box reappears, and the word "prefetch" (P R E F E T C H) in red text flashes as the user types "prefetch" into the "Open" field and clicks "OK." The "Prefetch" folder opens, showing many files. The text "Ctrl+A" in red flashes again as the user selects all files (Ctrl+A), right-clicks, and chooses "Delete," leaving the folder empty.

The video opens with a static shot of a Windows 10 desktop featuring a blue background with a light abstract pattern. Several application icons are neatly arranged on the left side of the screen, including "This PC," "Recycle Bin," "Google Chrome," "SHAREit," "Wondershare Filmora," "OBS," "Google Chrome," and "RAMESH 3997 ATS." The taskbar is visible at the bottom of the screen, displaying the time "11:26" and date "15/08/2017" in the bottom right corner. A logo consisting of intertwined red, orange, and yellow shapes with "TV" in white text and the tagline "The Power is Within" is positioned in the top right corner. In the bottom center, an orange rectangular box with white text appears, stating "07 Hide Windows Services."

The video opens with a Windows 10 desktop displaying a blue background with a stylized window icon. On the left side, several icons are visible, including "This PC," "Recycle Bin," and "Google Chrome." The taskbar at the bottom features various pinned application icons. In the bottom right corner, the date "15/08/2017" and time "11:27" are displayed. A "YOUSUF TV" logo is present in the top right. A text overlay in a yellow circle and pink banner reads "08 Regedit." A voiceover states, "step is Regedit." The user then clicks the Start button, opening the Windows Start Menu, which displays app tiles and sections like "Recently added" and "Life at a glance." The voiceover says, "To do that," before the Start Menu closes and the search bar appears. The user types "run" into the search bar, which shows "Best match" (Run - Desktop app) and "Search suggestions" (run - See with results, Settings). The voiceover continues, "type R U N on the search." Finally, the search bar disappears, and a "Run" dialog box opens on the desktop, displaying "Regedit" in the "Open:" text field, along with "OK," "Cancel," and "Browse" buttons. The voiceover concludes, "and open the run command."

The video opens on a Windows 10 desktop with a blue-hued wallpaper featuring the Windows logo. In the bottom-left corner, a "Run" dialog box is visible, displaying the text "regedit" in its "Open:" field. The cursor clicks the "OK" button in this dialog box, which then closes. Subsequently, the "Registry Editor" window appears, occupying the center of the screen. On the left pane of the "Registry Editor," a hierarchical list of registry keys is shown. The key "HKEY_CURRENT_USER" is highlighted in blue. The cursor then clicks the arrow next to "HKEY_CURRENT_USER," expanding it to reveal a list of sub-keys. The cursor navigates this expanded list and hovers over the "Control Panel" sub-key.

The video segment opens with a view of a Windows 10 desktop, featuring a dark blue background with a bright, stylized Windows logo. Several desktop icons are visible on the left side, including "This PC," "Recycle Bin," "Google Chrome," "SHAREit," "Wondershare Filmora," "Orbit," and "RAMESH 1997 ATS." A taskbar is present at the bottom, displaying a "Type here to search" bar, various application icons, and system information like the time "11:39 PM" and date "15/08/2017." A logo for "WinTV" with the tagline "The Power Is Within" is located in the top-right corner. The scene then transitions to a solid green background, where a small white square quickly expands into a white rectangular box. Inside this white box, text appears: "Easy Classes" in small green font, followed by "Thank You" in large green letters, "Like & Share" in blue, and "SUBSCRIBE" in prominent red text, outlined in green, with "FOR MORE VIDEOS" in green below it. A small red dot, resembling a mouse click, briefly appears near the bottom right of the white box as the "SUBSCRIBE" button is emphasized by a green rectangle.
